vedicHouse.12: expenses, distant places, retreat, spiritual life

combine6.detail: Your earthly branches form a six-harmony combination between the {ap} and {bp} pillars. While heavenly stems show how you come across on the surface, branches govern the grounded realities of daily life. Where these two pillars meet, your habits and instincts fit together quietly, giving you an easy, unforced rapport in that part of life.

mutual.detail: Each of you carries in abundance the very five-phase energy the other's chart needs for balance. Where either of you tends to tip or run thin on your own, the other's natural temperament steadies the scales. It is a rare configuration in BaZi synastry — simply being in each other's orbit helps both of you feel more grounded and whole.

one_way.detail: One person's chart is rich in the exact five-phase energy the other's chart needs to find balance. The one receiving that energy often feels calmer, clearer, and better backed simply by having the other around. Because that elemental boost flows mostly one way, it matters that the person providing it is seen, appreciated, and cared for in return.

clash.detail: Your day branches clash. In BaZi, the day branch is the most private chamber of the chart — how you unwind, your bodily rhythms, and what you need when your guard is down. At a polite distance the difference barely shows, but at close quarters or under the same roof your habits and tempos easily rub against each other, asking for a little extra breathing room on both sides.

combine6.detail: Your day branches form a six-harmony combination. The day branch holds who you are in private — your everyday rhythms and how you rest when no one is watching. Because these inner chambers fit together, being at close quarters feels effortless: even in quiet, ordinary hours, your paces match and the air between you feels settled and like home.

clash.detail: Your day stems, {sa} and {sb}, meet in a direct clash. Because day stems sit on the surface of the chart, this plays out in everyday reactions and speech: you approach things from opposite angles with the same directness, and when the pace picks up, small disagreements can easily turn into head-on collisions. Yet that very charge keeps the connection awake — neither of you can ever treat the other as background noise.

combine.detail: Your day stems, {sa} and {sb}, form one of the five combinations, leaning toward {el}. The day stem is the core of how each of you meets the world, and a stem combination always joins two different temperaments — one yin, one yang — that lock together on contact. There is an immediate ease between you, as if you already know how to read each other, and over time you naturally tilt toward one another's way of being.

controls.detail: Between the day stems {sa} and {sb}, one naturally restrains the other. In practice, one of you tends to set the frame, the standards, or the limits — which can feel like pressure or scrutiny when pushed too hard, yet also gives the other person structure, steadiness, and a clear edge to lean against. Everything depends on the lightness of the touch.

generates.detail: Between the day stems {sa} and {sb}, one naturally feeds and supports the other. One of you instinctively backs, steadies, and makes room for the other, who in turn finds firmer footing and an easier sense of safety in the relationship. So long as the one giving remembers to replenish their own energy, the warmth flows without effort.

same_element.detail: Your day stems ({sa} and {sb}) belong to the same element — what BaZi calls sharing the same qi. You are cut from similar cloth and understand each other's instincts and pride without needing a long explanation. The flip side of being so alike is that when you both dig in, neither of you is naturally inclined to yield first.

output_meets_power.detail: In your current ten-year luck pillars, one of you is moving through an Output decade — restless to express, question, and break out of old moulds — while the other is in an Officer decade defined by responsibility, pressure, and holding the line. You can balance each other well, one opening fresh air while the other keeps things anchored, yet when you are both stretched thin it is easy to pull in opposite directions at once.

sync.detail: Over the next ten years, your luck pillars move in the same general direction. Timing shapes a great deal of how two people get along: when your ten-year cycles run in step, you tend to want to push outward, take on new ground, or slow down and consolidate during the same seasons, without one of you having to wait for or drag the other along.

sole_element.detail: Looking at your two charts together, nearly all of the {el} between you comes from one person. In daily life, the qualities carried by {el} easily become that person's unspoken job for both of you. That creates a clear division of strengths, but it can also leave one person carrying the whole weight of that role — and leave a gap whenever they step back or run low.
sole_element.phrase: Nearly all {el} sits on one side

both_emotional.detail: Neither of you is wired for split-second certainty; with emotional authority on both sides, clarity only comes after you have ridden out the highs and lows of a feeling. Together, your moods can sometimes amplify each other—tempting you into rash promises on a shared high or making things look bleaker than they are on a low—and at other times your waves will simply be out of sync. The gift is that neither of you has to apologise for needing time. Letting big decisions wait until the waters have settled for both of you saves you from almost every regret.

wave_vs_instant.detail: When it comes to making a call, the two of you run on completely different clocks: one of you has to live with a choice through the highs and lows of a mood before the truth settles, while the other knows in a split second from a gut response or a flash of instinct. Without realising this, the fast decider feels stalled or confused when yesterday's answer shifts today, and the slower decider feels cornered into saying yes too soon—only to regret it by morning. Let the one who knows now register their first instinct, then give the other a night to sleep on it; the answer that survives until tomorrow is the one you can both trust.

companionship.detail: You each carry the whole of {channels} in your own chart. On the themes of this channel, you are wired the exact same way—there is no guesswork and no need to explain why you do what you do. It brings none of the drama of opposites, offering instead the quiet relief of recognition: a place where you naturally move at the same pace and understand each other without trying.

compromise.detail: On {channels}, one of you holds the entire channel while the other holds just one gate. This is one of the trickiest dynamics in a composite chart: the person with one end cares about this theme and brings their own way of doing part of it, yet repeatedly finds themselves bending to the other's fixed, already-complete way of operating. Often the one holding the full channel has no idea they are calling the shots, while the other quietly swallows frustration. Seeing the mechanics for what they are keeps a structural imbalance from feeling personal.

dominance.detail: One of you carries the whole of {channels}, while the other has neither end defined. Because the person who is open here has no fixed habit of their own to defend, this rarely turns into a tug-of-war; instead, it is a quality one person reliably brings to the table that the other can lean on, observe and learn from—so long as the open partner takes a breather when that constant energy starts to feel like too much.

many.detail: Across {channels}, each of you holds one half of the circuit, and only when you come together does the current flow. Being in the same room has a distinct charge to it—places where either of you might stall alone suddenly come alive in the other's company. The pull between you isn't built on sameness; it comes from each of you carrying the exact piece the other is missing.

some.detail: You each carry one end of {channels}, and together you bridge the gap. Around the themes of this channel, there is an immediate spark and curiosity between you—something that feels unfinished when you are on your own clicks into place the moment you engage with each other.

throat.detail: Several of your electromagnetic channels connect directly to the Throat centre, where inner thoughts and impulses turn into speech and tangible action. Ideas that either of you might sit on quietly when alone seem to spill out effortlessly once you start talking. Coming at things from different angles, you help each other finish the thought—making you a natural pair not just for lively conversation, but for turning half-formed plans into real work.

few.detail: Put your charts together and eight or all nine centres light up, leaving almost nothing undefined between you. As a pair you are remarkably self-contained—there is always something humming, and you rarely need outside company to feel complete. Yet a room with no open windows can start to feel airless after a while. Stepping apart for time on your own isn't distance; it is simply how each of you lets your open centres breathe and comes back to your own rhythm.
few.phrase: Nearly every centre lit up together

shared.detail: Even with your charts combined, four or more centres remain open between you. In those areas, neither of you imposes a fixed pattern on the other, giving the relationship plenty of breathing room and an unforced ease. Because neither of you anchors those themes, however, the surrounding environment and other people's moods can easily sweep you both up at once. Recognising when a wave of pressure comes from outside rather than from each other turns these open spaces into shared windows on the world.

manifestor_generator.detail: One of you is wired to get things moving from a standing start in bursts of independent energy; the other has the deep, steady reserves to carry something for the long haul once their gut says yes. You naturally divide into spark and stamina. Friction usually shows up at the handover: if the initiator leaps into action unannounced, the other feels steamrolled, while expecting the initiator to keep up a relentless daily grind only drains them. A simple heads-up before making a move gives the other person something real to respond to, turning two very different paces into a relay.

projector_generator.detail: One of you is built to see the big picture and guide how energy is spent; the other carries the steady engine to build and follow through. The catch is that both of you are wired to wait—one to be genuinely invited before sharing an insight, the other for something concrete to respond to from the gut. Left unbridged, unasked-for advice lands as criticism, and open-ended questions draw a blank. The whole dynamic unlocks once one remembers to ask for the other's perspective, and the other offers clear yes-or-no options to respond to.
projector_generator.phrase: Waiting for an invitation × waiting to respond

two_manifestors.detail: Neither of you is built to wait for permission or be managed; you both move when an inner urge strikes and guard your autonomy fiercely. The gift of this pairing is that you instinctively understand each other's need for freedom and quiet recovery without taking it personally. The flashpoint comes when you act around each other unannounced, setting off an instant, defensive pushback from both sides. Letting the other know what you are about to do isn't asking for approval—it is the simple courtesy that lowers the walls between two independent forces.

lifepath_lead_support.detail: One of you has a Life Path (1 or 8) wired for agency, direction, and getting things done; the other has a Life Path (2 or 6) wired for harmony, partnership, and looking after the people involved. One naturally pushes forward while the other holds the relationship together—a strong complement, so long as the louder driver leaves room to listen and the peacemaker doesn't always give way.

personal_year_same.detail: Within numerology's nine-year cycle, you are both in the same Personal Year right now. This year carries the same seasonal rhythm for you both—whether the pull is to start something fresh, put your heads down and build, or clear the decks and rest—so your timing for pushing ahead or slowing down naturally matches.

same_life_path.detail: You share the same Life Path number. In numerology, the Life Path points to the central theme and lessons that run through a person's life; having the same number means you recognise each other's drive and sticking points from the inside out. You rarely have to explain why something matters so much to you—the other person already gets it.

anxious_avoidant.detail: When tension or uncertainty creeps in, your instincts pull in opposite directions: one of you reaches for closeness and reassurance to feel safe again, while the other pulls back into their own space to settle down. That easily sets off a familiar loop — the more one reaches, the more crowded the other feels; the more the other retreats, the more alarmed the first becomes. Naming the pattern makes all the difference: when the one stepping back can say “I just need a breather, I’m still here,” neither of you has to get stuck in the chase.

both_anxious.detail: You both care deeply about closeness and pick up quickly on shifts in each other’s tone, warmth, or reply time. At your best, you are wonderfully attentive and generous with reassurance, because you both know what it means to feel held. The flip side is that a hectic day or an unexplained silence can rattle you both at once. Having a simple shorthand — like “swamped today, we’re good” — stops false alarms from snowballing.

both_avoidant.detail: You both prize your independence and tend to sort through heavy feelings on your own. Day to day, that makes things refreshingly low-pressure: neither of you crowds the other or takes a need for quiet personally. The only risk is becoming so self-sufficient that you drift into parallel tracks — so when something really weighs on you, it is worth resisting the urge to say “I’m fine” and letting the other person in.

secure_anchor.detail: One of you brings a secure attachment style to the relationship, giving the bond a steady home base. Being comfortable with closeness without feeling crowded — and able to handle distance without panicking — keeps everyday friction or busy spells from feeling like a threat to what you have, making it much easier to find your way back to each other after ups and downs.

conscientiousness_gap.detail: One of you likes things in order, takes commitments seriously, and feels best when a plan is seen through properly; the other moves more by feel, stays relaxed about structure, and prefers to improvise. Around shared tasks, timing, and everyday order, the first can start to feel they are carrying the load alone, while the second can feel policed. Agreeing on a few clear non-negotiables — and letting the rest be done each person’s own way — saves a lot of wear and tear.

neuroticism_gap.detail: One of you picks up on shifts and stresses early and feels them deeply, while the other stays on a fairly even keel when things get bumpy. That contrast can work well for you both: one notices subtle undercurrents, and the other offers a steady presence when storms hit. The key is for the steadier side not to wave off the other’s feelings as overthinking, and for the more sensitive side not to mistake calm for indifference.

both_dominance.detail: You both lead with Dominance (D) in DISC: you speak plainly, decide quickly, and naturally reach for the wheel when something needs doing. When you share a goal, you can move mountains together without wasting time tiptoeing around each other. When you disagree, though, neither of you is inclined to yield just to keep the peace, and things can quickly lock up. Dividing up who has the final say in which area keeps you from wrestling over the same wheel.
both_dominance.phrase: Both like to take the lead

pace_gap.detail: In your DISC styles, one of you likes to get moving quickly and adjust on the fly, while the other prefers to think things through and move at a measured, steady pace. Left unchecked, the faster side can feel held back, and the steadier side can feel rushed into half-baked calls. Giving a little breathing room to weigh things up — along with a clear time to make the call — lets momentum and care work together.

same_center.detail: Your Enneagram types belong to the same centre — whether gut, heart, or head, you take in the world through the same first radar. Even if your day-to-day habits differ, your gut reactions under pressure and the things you instinctively try to protect come from the same place, making it natural to understand why the other reacts the way they do.

ei_split.detail: When something comes up, one of you needs quiet time to sort through it privately before speaking, while the other figures out what they think by talking it through out loud. On the very same issue, one wants a pause and the other wants a conversation right now. Once you both see that silence is not shutting the other out and thinking aloud is not a final verdict, it becomes much easier to give each other that beat.
ei_split.phrase: Mull it over × talk it out

jp_split.detail: One of you relaxes once a decision is made and the plan is set, while the other feels most at ease keeping options open so you can adapt as things unfold. Schedules, trips, and deadlines bring the difference out into the open: one feels left hanging when things stay up in the air, and the other feels boxed in when pressed to commit too early. Knowing which decisions truly need locking down and which can stay flexible takes the edge off both of you.

shared_intuition.detail: You both lean toward Intuition (N) in the 16 Types. Conversations between you rarely stay on the surface of facts for long — you are both drawn to what sits behind things, where an idea might lead, and how one thought connects to another. One of you can toss out half a notion or a rough metaphor, and the other will pick up the thread without needing every step spelled out.

shared_sensing.detail: You both lean toward Sensing (S) in the 16 Types. Rather than trading abstract theories, you both trust what you have seen, done, and experienced firsthand. Whether you are working out a practical plan or catching up on life, you speak in concrete examples and real details, making it easy to understand each other without having to decode vague hints.

sn_split.detail: Faced with the same situation, one of you looks first for the underlying pattern and what could happen next, while the other looks for solid facts and how things actually work on the ground. In conversation, the first can feel the second is caught up in minutiae, and the second can feel the first is floating off into thin air — yet together, one watches the horizon while the other minds the footing, giving you the whole picture.

tf_split.detail: When making a call or working through a disagreement, one of you looks first at how it affects the people involved and how everyone feels, while the other looks at whether the logic holds up and the principle is sound. In a heated moment, the first can feel met with coldness, while the second can feel the actual point is being sidestepped — yet each of you is guarding half of what matters: getting the issue right, and looking after the people in it.

opposite_direction.detail: On the values circle, what each of you cares about most sits on opposite sides — for instance, one drawn to change and new ground while the other prizes stability and roots, or one focused on personal drive while the other looks out for the wider group. Each of you naturally watches the blind spot the other leaves unguarded. Before big decisions, asking what each of you is trying to protect turns a tug-of-war into a much fuller view.

shared_direction.detail: In the values questionnaire, what each of you puts first points in the same direction. That kinship shows up most in everyday trade-offs — what is worth spending time and energy on, what you will stand up for, and what kind of life feels well lived. Many of your choices need no long explanation, because the other already understands why they matter to you.

dasha_sync.detail: Your current major planetary periods (Mahadashas) are ruled by the same planet, or by planets that are natural friends. Because a Mahadasha sets the tone for a multi-year chapter of life, you are moving through similar weather right now—making it much easier to understand where the other person's energy is going and to keep a shared pace.

gana_low.detail: Your Moon nakshatras belong to different temperament groups (Gana). Traditionally, this points to contrasting baseline reflexes and ways of processing things—when something comes up, one of you may want to meet it head-on and sort it out immediately, while the other needs a gentler approach or time to let the dust settle. Giving each other room to digest things at your own speed goes a long way.

gana_match.detail: Your Moon nakshatras fall into the same or closely compatible temperament group (Gana). In Vedic tradition, Gana reflects your baseline temperament and reflex responses to daily life: when it matches, your everyday tempo—how fast you react, how you handle small irritations, and when you want company or quiet—tends to line up naturally.

graha_maitri_high.detail: The planetary rulers of your two Moon signs are on friendly terms (or are the same planet). Because the Moon in Vedic astrology governs how the mind takes in and responds to life, friendly rulers point to an easy mental rapport: you tend to follow each other's train of thought without needing much translation.

tara_high.detail: Counting from one Moon nakshatra to the other places each of you in a supportive position (Tara) in the Vedic lunar cycle. Traditionally, this is read as a quietly fortunate link: you tend to be a steadying, helpful presence in each other's lives, lending momentum and support when it counts.

yoni_high.detail: The animal symbols (Yoni) tied to your Moon nakshatras are the same or naturally friendly. In Vedic tradition, this speaks to an instinctive, sensory ease between two people—a feeling of being comfortable in your own skin around each other, with an unforced warmth that draws you together.

asc_asc_square.detail: Your Ascendants square or oppose each other. You meet the outside world with very different first reflexes: where one of you reaches for structure and a clear plan, the other reads the room and goes with the flow. In public or unfamiliar settings you can easily feel out of step, yet each of you brings the exact presence the other lacks.

jupiter_lifts.detail: One person’s Jupiter meets the other’s Sun or Moon in a conjunction or easy aspect. There is a generous, encouraging spirit to this contact: around each other, small slights are easily forgiven and bigger possibilities feel within reach. One of you naturally bolsters the other’s confidence, making the world feel wider when you are together.

mars_mars_tension.detail: Your two Mars placements square or oppose each other. Your instincts for how and when to act pull at cross-purposes: just as one of you wants to push straight ahead, the other wants to slow down or take a different tack. Everyday logistics can spark quick, sharp clashes, though there is a certain honesty to it—neither of you tiptoes around the other.

mercury_harmony.detail: Your Mercurys meet in a conjunction or easy aspect. Your minds work along compatible lines, so you catch each other’s drift, humour and logic without needing to spell everything out. Whether you are sorting out practical plans or talking late into the night, conversation flows easily between you.

mercury_tension.detail: Your Mercurys square or oppose each other. You gather thoughts and put them into words differently: one of you may focus on literal details while the other speaks in broad strokes, or one thinks out loud while the other only speaks once they are sure. Because you can easily talk past each other, it pays to pause and ask what the other actually meant.

moon_mc_conjunction.detail: One person’s Moon sits right on the other’s Midheaven (within {orb}°). One of you instinctively takes the other’s ambitions, reputation and life in the world to heart, offering quiet emotional backing where they are most visible; the other feels genuinely understood and held in what they are trying to build out there.

moon_moon_harmony.detail: Your Moons meet in a conjunction or easy aspect. Because the Moon governs everyday habits and emotional reflexes, you unwind in similar ways and reach for the same kind of comfort when life gets heavy. Much of what you feel goes without saying between you, making day-to-day life together feel easy and unforced.

moon_moon_tension.detail: Your Moons square or oppose each other. When you are tired or upset, your emotional reflexes pull in different directions: one may need to talk things through straight away while the other retreats into quiet, or one offers practical fixes when the other just wants warmth. Even with the best intentions, the comfort you instinctively give isn’t always the comfort the other needs.

node_contact.detail: One person’s Sun, Moon or Venus sits on the other’s North Node. Because the North Node points toward the life a person is still learning to grow into, the planet person naturally embodies qualities the other is trying to develop. This connection often acts as a catalyst, nudging one of you past old habits toward a future you quietly want.

overlay_7th.detail: One person’s Sun, Moon or Venus falls in the other’s 7th house. Because the 7th house shapes what a person looks for in a true one-to-one partner, the house person instinctively recognises the other as someone meant to sit across the table from them—not just in passing, but as a genuine counterpart.

pluto_personal.detail: One person’s Pluto meets the other’s Sun, Moon or Venus in a conjunction or hard aspect. Nothing about this pull is casual: you seem to see straight past each other’s defences, creating an intense, absorbing bond. Because that depth can also stir possessiveness or quiet struggles over who holds the upper hand, naming fears and boundaries openly matters here more than usual.

saturn_moon.detail: One person’s Saturn meets the other’s Moon in a conjunction or hard aspect. This brings real weight and staying power to the bond—neither of you takes the other lightly. Yet when feelings are raw, the Moon person can feel judged, cooled down or managed, while the Saturn person can feel cast as the responsible one who always has to hold things together.

saturn_sun_venus_soft.detail: One person’s Saturn forms a conjunction or easy aspect with the other’s Sun or Venus. Here Saturn brings quiet reliability rather than weight: promises are kept, trust builds steadily over time, and the bond doesn’t depend on constant excitement to hold together. You are well suited to building things that take patience and follow-through.

sun_mars_harmony.detail: One person’s Sun forms an easy angle with the other’s Mars. Ideas rarely stay on the shelf for long between you: one person’s sense of purpose feeds straight into the other’s drive to act. Whether you are tackling a project or backing each other up, you each feel bolder and more decisive with the other in your corner.

sun_moon_harmony.detail: One person’s Sun meets the other’s Moon in a conjunction or easy aspect. Who one of you is at your core naturally makes the other feel safe and at home, while the Moon person’s instinctive warmth lets the Sun person drop their guard and feel wholly accepted. There is an effortless sense of holding each other up.

uranus_venus_moon.detail: One person’s Uranus meets the other’s Venus or Moon in a conjunction or hard aspect. There is a live-wire freshness between you that shakes both of you out of routine and convention. Yet closeness can feel erratic if either person feels boxed in: this bond thrives when you leave plenty of room for independence and the unexpected.

venus_mars_harmony.detail: One person’s Venus meets the other’s Mars in a conjunction or easy aspect. This is one of astrology’s classic signatures of chemistry: the way one of you expresses warmth and charm naturally draws out the other’s desire and initiative. Affection and playfulness come easily between you, without either person having to try too hard.

venus_mars_tension.detail: One person’s Venus squares or opposes the other’s Mars. The magnetism between you is strong—often electric—but it comes with an edge. Your timing around affection and desire doesn’t always line up: one may want unhurried tenderness just when the other comes on fast, creating a recurring tug between pulling closer and needing breathing room.

ji_into_ming.detail: One person’s birth-year Obstruction transformation (Hua Ji) lands in the other’s Life or Partner palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, Hua Ji is less about simple obstacle than about fixation, deep attachment and what the heart cannot easily set down. When it falls here, the first person finds it almost impossible to take the second person lightly: they worry, notice every small shift and hold on tight. That intensity creates an unmistakable bond, yet when care turns into anxious scrutiny, the second person can feel crowded or weighed down—making breathing room just as important as closeness.

lu_into_ming.detail: One person’s birth-year Prosperity transformation (Hua Lu) lands in the other’s Life or Partner palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, Hua Lu marks where a person’s natural warmth, generosity and goodwill flow most freely. When it falls into these core palaces of the second person’s chart, the first person instinctively wants to give, accommodate and bring ease to the other without keeping score—and the second person can feel that warmth directly, experiencing the relationship as a place where they are genuinely cared for.

ming_in_fude.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Fortune palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, the Fortune palace is the seat of a person’s inner life—their quiet joys, emotional baseline and mental rest. When the first person’s Life palace lands here, their very presence reaches the second person’s inner world. Around them, the second person feels little need to put on a front; tension eases, the mind settles, and even ordinary quiet time together feels restorative.
ming_in_fude.phrase: Life palace in the Fortune palace

ming_in_fumu.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Parents palace. Beyond literal parents, this palace in Zi Wei Dou Shu represents shelter, guidance and the kind of authority that comes with care. Regardless of your actual ages, the first person carries a steady, mentor-like weight in the second person’s eyes. The first person is naturally inclined to look out for and guide the second, and when the second person is unsure of their footing, advice or reminders from the first tend to sink in where others’ might not.
ming_in_fumu.phrase: Life palace in the Parents palace

ming_in_fuqi.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Partner palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, the Partner palace holds a person’s instinctive picture of intimacy and companionship. When the first person’s Life palace sits right in that space, who they naturally are matches the shape of what the second person is drawn to. Often from early on, before either of you has tried very hard, the second person feels an unspoken familiarity and pull—as though a place for this person was already waiting in their life.
ming_in_fuqi.phrase: Life palace in the Partner palace

ming_in_guanlu.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Career palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, the Career palace governs direction, work and how a person puts plans into action, forming part of the core triad with the Life palace. Because the first person’s Life palace sits here, their way of thinking and getting things done naturally earns the second person’s trust. Whether you are working together, planning ahead or tackling a practical problem in daily life, the first person brings steadiness and momentum to the second person’s goals.
ming_in_guanlu.phrase: Life palace in the Career palace

ming_in_peers.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Siblings or Friends palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, these two palaces form the axis of peers, close allies and companions on equal footing. Whatever your formal roles in life—whether partners, family or colleagues—the second person naturally experiences the first as a peer and confidant. There is very little ceremony or hierarchy between you: conversation is candid, easy and on the level, much like two good friends walking side by side.
ming_in_peers.phrase: Life palace in a peer palace

ming_in_resources.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Wealth or Property palace. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, the Wealth palace governs practical resources and how value is handled, while the Property palace represents home, roots and the spaces where daily life is lived. Having the first person’s Life palace land here ties them directly into the tangible foundations of the second person’s life. Your connection grounds itself easily in the everyday—whether that means managing resources, sharing a roof or steadily building something lasting together.
ming_in_resources.phrase: Life palace in a resource palace

mutual_qianyi.detail: Each person’s Life palace falls directly in the other’s Travel palace, making your Life–Travel axes mirror images of one another. In Zi Wei Dou Shu, the Travel palace governs horizons, movement and the world beyond familiar ground. You act as each other’s window onto a wider world: what is everyday territory for one is fresh country for the other. Together, you naturally draw each other out of old routines, introducing new places, ideas and possibilities that neither of you might have stepped into alone.

attraction.describes: What pulls you towards each other and makes you want to get close.
attraction.name: Attraction

communication.describes: How easily you talk things through and understand what the other means.
communication.name: Communication

emotion.describes: How you tune in to each other’s moods and care for one another.
emotion.name: Emotional bond

growth.describes: How being around each other shapes and changes you over time.
growth.name: Growth

rhythm.describes: Whether you move at a similar pace when deciding, acting and resting.
rhythm.name: Rhythm

values.describes: What matters most to each of you, and how well your priorities line up.
values.name: Values

friction.body: You can hardly ignore each other, yet getting close is rarely straightforward. Often, the exact trait you first admired in the other person becomes the most frustrating thing to deal with in everyday life; or just as one of you takes a step closer, the other instinctively pulls back a little. There is no lack of pull between you, only a need for a bit of breathing room so you do not crowd each other.
friction.practice: Name one trait in the other that you both admire and occasionally find maddening, and compare notes on when it tips from one to the other.
friction.quote: The very quality that draws you to each other is often what tests your patience up close.

quiet.body: When you first met, neither of you probably felt an overwhelming pull, and neither of you had to try hard to impress the other. Yours is a slow-warming bond: familiarity and trust grow quietly out of ordinary hours spent together and things lived through side by side. It may lack sudden excitement at the start, but it makes up for it in comfort and steadiness over time.
quiet.practice: Spend an hour somewhere neither of you usually goes — an unfamiliar neighbourhood or a different café — and see what you notice about each other outside your usual routine.
quiet.quote: You are not the type to set off instant fireworks, which makes being together easy and unforced.

strong.body: Whether it is because you recognise something familiar in each other or because the other person has qualities you lack, your attention naturally goes to them when you are together. You genuinely want to know what they think and how they do things. That effortless interest makes it easy to get close — though in the beginning it can also make you idealise each other a little before you see the whole picture.
strong.practice: Tell each other about one specific moment recently when you looked at the other and thought, “That is so unmistakably you.”
strong.quote: You are naturally drawn to each other and genuinely curious about how the other ticks.

friction.body: You have different habits in conversation: one of you might think out loud while the other takes every passing remark as a final decision; or one focuses strictly on the facts while the other reacts to tone of voice. When talks go wrong between you, it is rarely because you fundamentally disagree — it is usually because the way something was phrased rubbed the other the wrong way, turning the conversation into an argument over “what you meant by that”.
friction.practice: When a conversation starts to heat up, pause for a moment and check what you heard in plain words: “So what you’re saying is… Have I got that right?”
friction.quote: Even when talking about the same thing, your different ways of speaking and listening can easily cause misunderstandings.

quiet.body: You are not the kind of pair who never run out of things to talk about, and sitting in the same room without chatting feels completely comfortable. That ease with silence is restful, though if you are not careful, your conversations can shrink down to practicalities and daily errands. Neither of you can read minds, so if something is on your mind, you have to take the initiative and bring it up.
quiet.practice: Over a meal or a walk, set everyday errands aside and ask each other: “What’s something you’ve been thinking about a lot lately?”
quiet.quote: You do not need constant conversation when you are together, so what matters needs to be said out loud.

strong.body: You rarely need long explanations to catch each other’s meaning, and even when the conversation jumps from one subject to another, you both keep up naturally. The only trap in understanding each other so quickly is assuming you are on the same page about complex or sensitive matters without actually spelling out the details, only to find out later that you had different things in mind.
strong.practice: Next time you agree quickly on something important, pause and ask: “Just so we’re sure, what does this actually look like in practice to you?”
strong.quote: Talking comes easily between you — half a sentence is often enough for the other to get the point.

friction.body: Under stress, your instincts often pull in opposite directions: one of you might want to talk things through right away while the other wants to be left alone for a while; or one jumps straight into fixing the problem when the other just wants a sympathetic ear. Hurt feelings between you rarely come from a lack of care — they happen when you offer the kind of comfort you would want, rather than what the other person actually needs.
friction.practice: While you are both in a good mood, tell each other plainly for harder days: “When I’m in a bad mood or overwhelmed, what helps me most from you is…”
friction.quote: When one of you is upset, you deal with feelings and show care in very different ways.

quiet.body: When something bothers you, your first instinct is usually to deal with it yourself rather than unloading it onto the other person. That keeps your relationship steady and free of emotional drama. Because you are both so self-contained and polite with boundaries, though, you can sometimes keep each other at arm’s length; deeper closeness takes time and grows as you go through hard moments together and let your guard down.
quiet.practice: Next time something leaves you slightly frustrated or unsure, try mentioning it to the other before you have neatly sorted it out on your own.
quiet.quote: You each tend to sort through your feelings on your own, keeping your time together light and low-pressure.

strong.body: You are naturally sensitive to how the other is doing — when one of you is tired or weighed down by something, the other usually notices before a word is said. Being around each other makes it easy to let your guard down. Because you feel each other’s moods so keenly, though, one person’s bad day can easily bring the other down too. Keeping your own footing helps you support each other better.
strong.practice: Recall one small, specific thing the other did recently that made you feel looked after, and tell them about it.
strong.quote: You pick up on each other’s moods right away, and neither of you has to put on a brave face when you are together.

friction.body: Each of you tends to see right through the excuses the other makes, pushing the other to face things they would rather brush aside. That honesty helps you both grow fast, but nobody wants to feel constantly corrected or pushed. Not every moment between you needs to be about self-improvement — knowing when to drop the critique and simply accept each other as you are gives the relationship room to breathe.
friction.practice: Once this week, when you spot the other slipping into a familiar habit you would normally point out, consciously let it pass without comment or advice.
friction.quote: You easily spot each other’s blind spots and push each other to improve, though it can be tiring if you never let up.

quiet.body: There is very little pressure between you to critique, coach, or push each other to improve. Life outside demands plenty of effort already; around each other, you take one another as you are and offer a place to rest. When it comes to personal goals and self-improvement, you each pursue your own path at your own pace without needing to drag the other along.
quiet.practice: Share one personal project or goal each of you is working on right now — not for advice, just so the other knows what you are up to and can cheer you on.
quiet.quote: Neither of you is trying to fix or remould the other, so you can simply be yourselves when you are together.

strong.body: What one of you struggles with is often something the other handles with ease. Better still, you lend each other a hand naturally without making the other person feel small. Just be careful not to rely so completely on the other’s strong points that you stop trying yourself — pay attention to how they handle things, and let some of their strengths rub off on you.
strong.practice: Tell the other about one habit or way of handling things that you used to struggle with, but have gotten much better at since knowing them.
strong.quote: Your strengths complement each other well, and over time you both pick up new skills from being around the other.

friction.body: When something comes up, the quicker one wants to settle it and get moving right away, easily growing impatient with delays; the slower one needs time to think things through and hates feeling rushed. Neither pace is wrong — speed gets things off the ground, and caution catches mistakes. Instead of pulling at each other to move at the same speed, build a time buffer into how you do things: let the faster one scout ahead, and let the slower one review and refine.
friction.practice: When a joint decision comes up, let the quicker one put the options on the table first, then agree on a clear time — say, tomorrow evening — to decide, with no nudging in between.
friction.quote: You decide and act at different speeds — one of you likes to move fast, while the other takes their time.

quiet.body: Your everyday rhythms neither match beat for beat nor clash with each other. Most of the time, you can comfortably get on with your own things without feeling the need to do everything in lockstep. As long as you agree clearly on the times when your schedules actually need to meet, leaving the rest of the day to each person’s own pace keeps things easy for both of you.
quiet.practice: Spend an hour this week in the same room doing your own separate things — reading, working, or relaxing — and enjoy the ease of unforced company.
quiet.quote: You each keep your own routine and pace, without getting in each other’s way.

strong.body: From how quickly you make up your minds and run errands to the moment at a gathering when you are both ready to head home, you move at a very similar speed. Living or working together feels smooth because nobody feels rushed and nobody is left waiting. The only downside is that two people moving at the same tempo can easily overwork together or put off the same chore together, so someone needs to keep an eye on the time now and then.
strong.practice: Notice whether the two of you have been non-stop busy lately or putting something off together — and either set aside an afternoon to rest, or take half an hour to clear that task side by side.
strong.quote: Whether you are getting things done or taking a break, your everyday paces match naturally.

friction.body: Looking at the same situation, one of you may care most about stability and certainty while the other wants freedom and fresh possibilities; or one focuses on efficiency and results while the other cares more about how people feel along the way. What looks like an argument over a small practical detail is usually a clash between these deeper priorities. You do not need to convert each other — once you understand what the other person is most worried about losing, it becomes much easier to find a middle ground.
friction.practice: Pick one issue where you lean different ways, set solutions aside for five minutes, and each answer: “If we do it entirely your way, what I’m most worried about is…”
friction.quote: When making a choice, you often care about different things and put them in a different order.

quiet.body: Your priorities neither match completely nor clash head-on. That gives your relationship plenty of breathing room: each of you can care about your own interests and standards without needing the other to follow suit. When a decision does involve both of you, there is no need to debate big principles — simply working things out case by case is enough.
quiet.practice: Next time you are making a shared plan, each name the single requirement you care about most, and stay flexible on the rest.
quiet.quote: Even when you care about different things in life, you can easily respect each other’s ways and get along well.

strong.body: From everyday choices about time and money to deeper principles about how to treat people and get things done, you care about very similar things. You rarely have to argue over basic priorities, which makes joint decisions straightforward. The only catch is that when two people look at a problem from the exact same angle, they tend to miss the exact same blind spots — so on big decisions, it helps to ask for an outside view.
strong.practice: Look back at a choice you made together recently and ask: knowing what we know now, would we still choose the same way, or did we both overlook something?
strong.quote: You see eye to eye on what is worth taking seriously and what can be let go.

closeness_vs_space.practice: Make a two-part pact: the one stepping back always offers reassurance and a return time before disappearing, and the one feeling uneasy asks for a quick “we’re okay” straight out instead of testing the waters.
closeness_vs_space.scene: When life gets heavy or tense, you recharge in opposite ways. One of you reaches out for connection to feel steady again; the other needs to unplug and retreat into their own corner. The further one pulls back, the harder the other reaches in — and the tighter the knot gets.

closer.inner: When you suddenly go quiet and distant, my mind starts spinning stories that something’s wrong between us. I’m not trying to crowd you — I just need to know we’re all right.
closer.say: “I’m feeling a bit wobbly because you’re quiet — just tell me we’re good, and I’ll happily leave you to have your space.”

spacer.inner: My battery is just flat — it’s not about you at all. But when you keep coming after me for a reaction, I feel suffocated and have nothing left to give.
spacer.say: “We’re completely fine, I promise. I’m just running on empty today — give me an hour to myself to recharge, and then I’ll come and find you.”

closeness_vs_space.title: Reaching in, pulling back

control_vs_yield.practice: Ban the phrase “I don’t mind” for a week: the one who usually leads holds back their own preference until the other has spoken first, and the one who usually yields practises naming even a small preference out loud.
control_vs_yield.scene: Without either of you meaning to, you’ve fallen into a set pattern: one of you naturally takes the wheel, and the other says “I don’t mind, up to you.” On the surface it looks effortless, until all those unspoken preferences quietly pile up into resentment.

leads.inner: I step in and decide because I want things sorted and you never seem to mind — I genuinely didn’t realise you were biting your tongue to keep the peace.
leads.say: “I realise I’m always the one calling the shots here. I’m biting my tongue this time — don’t say ‘easy either way’, tell me what you’d actually like.”

yields.inner: You always seem so sure of what you want that pushing back feels like more trouble than it’s worth. So I go along with it — and then quietly feel like there’s no room for me here.
yields.say: “Usually I just go with the flow, but I actually do care about this one. Can we try it my way this time?”

control_vs_yield.title: One drives, the other goes along

decision_pace.practice: Separate first impressions from the final call: the faster one shares where they’re leaning straight away, the slower one names a time they’ll come back with an answer, and in between, nobody nudges.
decision_pace.scene: Something comes up that needs a decision. One of you knows where you stand almost instantly and wants it settled; the other needs to sit with it and see how it feels tomorrow. Soon one of you feels held up in mid-air, and the other feels backed into a corner.

fast.inner: My gut already knows. Leaving it up in the air drains me, and it feels like the window is closing while we sit here hesitating.
fast.say: “I know what I’d like to do, so I’ll put my vote on the table. Take the time you need — just tell me when we can revisit it.”

slow.inner: I’m not stalling on purpose. Right now my head is noisy — if you push me for an answer on the spot, I’ll either say yes just to end the conversation and regret it later, or say no out of sheer self-defence.
slow.say: “I can’t tell how I feel about it yet. Let me sleep on it — I’ll give you a proper answer tomorrow morning.”

decision_pace.title: Decide now, or sleep on it

direct_clash.practice: When you’re both in a good mood, pick a slightly ridiculous code word for “brakes”. Whenever either of you uses it mid-argument, you both stop talking for five minutes and change rooms before trying again.
direct_clash.scene: It usually starts over nothing much at all. You both have quick reflexes, so a slight edge in one voice draws an instant edge from the other. Within three sentences, you’re no longer talking about the original issue — you’re pushing back against how the other just spoke to you.

either.inner: I wasn’t trying to pick a fight; I just wanted to make my point. Then your tone felt like a shove, and everything in me automatically shoved back.
either.say: “Hold on — we’re just sparring now. Let’s take five minutes to cool off and start that again.”

direct_clash.title: Sparks when the pace picks up

processing_style.practice: Label the moment before it starts: the outward processor says upfront, “I’m just thinking out loud — no reply needed yet,” or the inward processor takes twenty quiet minutes first with a clear promise of when they’ll come back to talk.
processing_style.scene: When something rattles you, one of you sorts it out by talking — tossing half-formed thoughts into the air to see what makes sense. The other has to go quiet first to untangle it inside. One feels like they’re talking to a brick wall; the other feels flooded and cornered.

inward.inner: My head is still full of static. I can’t hear my own thoughts while you’re talking at me, and if I speak before I’ve sorted it out inside, it’ll come out wrong.
inward.say: “I’m not shutting you out — I just need half an hour of quiet to get my thoughts straight, and then I’m all yours.”

outward.inner: Thoughts stay tangled in my head until I hear myself say them out loud. What I’m saying right now is just a rough draft — when you go silent, it feels like you’ve walked out of the room.
outward.say: “I just need to think out loud for ten minutes to clear my head. You don’t need to fix it or have an answer ready.”

processing_style.title: Think it through, or talk it out

same_element_rivalry.practice: Stop sharing the same steering wheel: either divide the turf clearly so each of you owns different areas, or take turns being fully in charge while the other sits back without back-seat driving.
same_element_rivalry.scene: You don’t clash here because you’re different — you clash because you’re cut from the same cloth. Like two head chefs in one small kitchen, you both have strong instincts on the exact same turf, and neither is wired to take a back seat.

either.inner: I know exactly how this should be done, and biting my tongue while you do it differently goes against every bone in my body — besides, you’re just like me, so why am I the one expected to bend?
either.say: “We’re both too stubborn to share the steering wheel on this. Take the lead this time and I’ll stay out of your way — next one’s mine.”

same_element_rivalry.title: Too alike to back down

structure_vs_flow.practice: Agree on the bones and protect the gaps: lock in the two or three non-negotiable anchors early so the planner can rest easy, and deliberately ring-fence pockets of unscheduled time where nothing gets booked.
structure_vs_flow.scene: Whether it’s a weekend away or a shared project, one of you can only relax once the key pieces are in the diary; the other feels boxed in by a fixed schedule and wants to see what the day brings. One feels left carrying all the admin; the other feels managed.

improviser.inner: When every hour is spoken for days in advance, it stops feeling like life and starts feeling like a checklist. I need some blank space to breathe and follow the mood.
improviser.say: “Tell me which bits really matter to have settled now — let’s lock those in, and keep a big pocket of time with nothing planned.”

planner.inner: I’m not trying to control everything — it’s just that unmade plans hum in the back of my head. Once the big pieces are sorted, I can actually switch off and enjoy myself.
planner.say: “Let’s just nail down the one or two things that actually need booking so I can relax, and leave the rest of the time completely open.”

structure_vs_flow.title: Lock it in, or see how it goes

who_speaks_first.practice: If you’re the one who usually jumps in, make “What do you see here?” your first move before acting. If you’re the one who waits, knock on the door first: ask if they’d like your take before giving it.
who_speaks_first.scene: You’re looking at the same problem. One of you already sees what’s going on, but holds back until genuinely asked; the other either charges ahead alone or assumes that anyone with an opinion would just speak up. One ends up feeling overlooked, the other feels left to carry the ball alone.

initiates.inner: When I have a thought, I just say it — so when you’re quiet, I assume you don’t mind either way, or that I should just get on with it.
initiates.say: “I’m already running ahead with this — stop me for a second. What are you seeing that I’m missing?”

waits.inner: I can see where this is heading, but I know from experience that if I offer my view before you’re actually open to it, it either bounces right off or sounds like criticism.
waits.say: “I’ve got a few thoughts on this — are you in a place to hear them right now?”

who_speaks_first.title: Waiting to be asked, forgetting to ask

west.conventions: Natal houses use {houseSystem}; annual profections (the yearly time-lord technique) count whole signs from the Ascendant's sign instead. Triplicity rulers follow Dorotheus (by day, by night, participating — fire: Sun, Jupiter, Saturn; earth: Venus, Moon, Mars; air: Saturn, Mercury, Jupiter; water: Venus, Mars, Moon); under William Lilly's dignity score (domicile 5, exaltation 4, triplicity 3, term 2, face 1), only the triplicity ruler of the chart's own sect earns the 3 points. Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto are given their modern signs (Aquarius, Pisces, Scorpio) for dignity, while the chart ruler and dominant planet use the traditional rulers. Dominant element, mode, and planet use the engine's own weighting, as no tradition fixes one: Sun, Moon, and Ascendant count 3; Midheaven, Mercury, Venus, and Mars 2; Jupiter and Saturn 1.5; Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto 1. A dominant element or mode is named only when it leads the next-highest by at least 5 percentage points. A stellium requires at least four planets in one sign or house (at least one of them the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, or Mars), or at least three planets all conjunct one another; groups made up solely of slow outer planets, shared by everyone born in the same months, are not counted.

vedic.conventions: Rāhu and Ketu are calculated using {node}, casting an aspect to the 7th sign from their position only (another school also counts the 5th and 9th signs). Both Vimśottarī and Yoginī daśā years are 365.25 days. Functional natures for the ascendant (Lagna) follow the general rules of Bṛhat Parāśara Horā Śāstra (BPHS) ch. 34: lords of the 1st, 5th and 9th houses are benefic; lords of the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 11th are malefic unless they also rule a trine; the Sun and Moon carry no fault as 8th lords (34.7), while an 8th lord also ruling the 3rd, 7th or 11th counts as difficult (matching the chapter's ascendant lists); where the ascendant lists (34.19–44) read a planet differently, both readings are shown. Periods are graded into five bands from the planet's functional role, house, dignity, companions and yogas (BPHS 34 and 48; Phaladīpikā ch. 20), with sub-periods also weighed by their placement from the main-period planet (Phaladīpikā 20.29). Yogas appear as formed, weak or broken: Rāja yoga is broken when both lords also rule the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 34.15) and weak when a participant sits in the 6th, 8th or 12th, is debilitated, combust or lost a planetary war; Gaja-Kesarī follows BPHS 36.3 (counted from the ascendant or Moon, with a benefic joining or aspecting Jupiter, and broken by debilitation, combustion or a hostile sign using natural friendship from BPHS ch. 3); Budha-Āditya is weak when Mercury is combust; debilitation is cancelled by any condition in Phaladīpikā 7.26–30; planetary war follows Sūrya Siddhānta 7.19–21 (within one degree, the northern planet prevails). Sade Sati is graded by Saturn's benefic points in its transit sign (Phaladīpikā 26.41), its dignity (26.31), Jupiter's aspect (26.30) and Saturn's role for the ascendant.
